# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 9 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_009_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 1

**1** The third vision I saw, brothers and sisters, was this. **2** After I had fasted often and prayed to the Lord to show me the revelation he had promised through the aged woman — that very night she appeared to me and said: "Because you are so persistent and eager to know everything, come out to the field where you farm, and around the fifth hour I will appear to you and show you what you need to see." **3** I asked, "Which part of the field, my lady?" "Wherever you prefer," she replied. "Only choose a quiet spot." And before I could say another word to designate the location, she said, "I will come wherever you are." **4** I went to the field, brothers and sisters, counted the hours, and arrived at the place. I saw an ivory couch there, with a linen pillow on it and a fine linen covering spread over it. **5** When I found these things lying there with no one around, I was struck with wonder; a trembling came upon me and my hair stood on end. When I pulled myself together, I saw the aged woman approaching with a book in her hand. She sat down alone and greeted me: "Greetings, man of God." I was filled with deep grief and broke into tears. **6** She asked, "Why are you weeping?" I said, "Because, my lady, I do not know whether I will be able to endure to the end." She answered, "Be confident — you have been appointed by the Lord to endure the trials of this world, for your own sake and for the sake of your household. Take courage." **7** I said, "Lady, show me the vision." She replied, "Do you want to see it right now?" "Yes, my lady, I am greatly longing for it," I said. She reached out to me and touched me, and I felt as though I had just come from a bath. **8** "Come," she said. And I saw before me the things I had described — the great tower being built with brilliant squared stones.

---

*LOGOS note: "man of God" is a significant honorific (cf. 1 Tim 6:11; 2 Tim 3:17) — Hermas is being commissioned as a prophetic figure here.*
